visual_text: Mouth care and pneumonia: the evidence is uncertain
14 US nursing homes, 2,152 residents: no clear fall in pneumonia over 2 years
Cochrane 2022, 6 trials, all high risk of bias: effect largely unclear
Two small trials: fewer pneumonia deaths at 2 years (low certainty); a larger study: no clear difference at 18 months
No trial compared mouth care with none
Removes plaque, the main cause of tooth decay and gum disease
Sore spots and broken teeth found early
Zimmerman et al., JAMA Netw Open 2020; Cao et al., Cochrane 2022
alt_text: Comparison card. Left: trials of mouth care and pneumonia are uncertain: 14 US nursing homes showed no clear fall; Cochrane 2022 found six trials, all at high risk of bias; none compared mouth care with none. Right, marked as judgement: reasons to clean mouths anyway are plaque removal, comfort, easier eating, early detection of sore spots and dignity.
design_instructions: Comparison card: white column with lung icon (trial findings) and mint column with toothbrush icon (judgement). Headline with orange 'uncertain'. Claim C13-14-a and Cochrane 2022 claims. No people.
